hints: Look closely at the left side of the graph at very low substrate concentration. Which enzyme, P or Q, shoots up and levels off (reaches its Vmax) first?

Remember that Km is the substrate concentration needed to reach half of Vmax. If an enzyme needs only a little substrate to get going, is its Km low or high, and what does that tell you about affinity?
walkthrough:
**Observe what the curves are telling us**

Look at enzyme Q first. It rises very steeply and then becomes flat at a low substrate concentration.

Enzyme P rises more slowly and keeps climbing for much longer, so it needs a lot more substrate to approach its maximum rate.

**Recall what Km and affinity really mean**

Km is defined as the substrate concentration that gives half the maximum rate:
$$K_m = \text{substrate concentration at } \frac{V_{max}}{2}$$

A low Km means you need only a little substrate to reach half speed, so the enzyme grabs the substrate very easily. That means low Km = high affinity.

**Compare P and Q and choose**

Because Q reaches its plateau (its Vmax) much earlier, its half-Vmax point must also be at a lower substrate concentration than P's.

So enzyme Q has a lower Km than enzyme P, and therefore a higher affinity for the same substrate. That matches option C.

options.A: Incorrect because Q reaches half Vmax sooner, so its Km is lower not higher, and lower Km means higher not lower affinity logic is mixed up here.
options.B: Incorrect because although lower affinity does pair with higher Km, enzyme Q actually has the lower Km, not the higher Km.
options.C: Correct because enzyme Q plateaus at a lower substrate concentration, so its Km is lower, and a lower Km means a higher affinity for the substrate.
options.D: Incorrect because a lower Km always means a higher affinity, not a lower affinity, so these two terms contradict each other.
